title: Inference economics audit checklist — draft
content:
Purpose:
Quick working checklist and notes for the internal audit of the Optimize cost model assumptions. Meant to capture data sources, calibration steps we actually ran, open questions for finance sign-off, and next steps. Not polished — iterative working doc for the review session with Finance on 2025-02-12.

Summary of scope (short):
- Model: Optimize v2 cost model (token-unit economics + tail latency impact on batching).
- Outputs we care about: per-request marginal cost, steady-state cost per 1M tokens, recommended quantization profiles per workload tier, expected latency SLO breach rate under proposed batching.
- Calibration exercise: match historical hosted API billing + Dedicated committed usage for Q4 2024 and Jan 2025 test windows.

Data sources inventory (what we used and why):
- Token counts: aggregated from billing-raw.tokens_daily_export (BigQuery) — we sampled customer cohorts by plan tier. Caveat: pre-tokenization vs post-tokenization mismatch for some non-UTF8 content; we applied tokenizer-normalization script (linked above).
- Model throughput / perf: measured from perf-runs/benchmark-suite (S3 snapshots). These are wall-clock throughput numbers on prod GPU types (A10G, H100 lookalikes). Need to confirm whether Dedicated runs used same instance types; some Dedicated units used older A100 machines.
- GPU cost input: finance-infra/rate-cards-2024.json (public cloud + committed discounts). For Dedicated we used committed pricing for reserved instances; for hosted we used on-demand blended numbers. Note: discount schedules for 2025 renewals not included.
- Storage / KV cache cost: derived from infra-metrics/cache-hit-rates and estimated mem footprint per model shard. This is a model-based estimate (see 'assumptions on KV sizing' below).
- Networking: ingress negligible, egress estimated at $0.05/GB; pulled from cloud bills bucket. We included cross-region fallback egress for <1% of requests.
- Ops costs: SRE & infra ops allocation based on headcount attribution model (see finance link). We included 10% allocation to Optimize feature team — open to finance pushback.

Key assumptions and how we calibrated them (deltas flagged):
1) Batch size distribution: assumed 80% single-stream (interactive) and 20% batched (micro-batched 2–8) for product customers. Calibrated against request traces from prod-traces/interactive-vs-batch.csv. Delta: enterprise bench accounts show 40% batch — impacts unit cost by ~6%.
2) KV cache hit rate: baseline 27% for prefix caching using recent-window heuristic; sensitivity run at 10% and 50%. Source: cache-metrics/2024-11-to-2025-01. Uncertainty high because we only measured for a subset of models and token lengths.
3) Latency SLO effect on batching: we assume that interactive requests must be prioritized and cannot be delayed >50ms; thus batching window effectively limited to 15ms for interactive path. This reduces achievable batch amortization on token compute by ~12%. This is our conservative assumption; needs product sign-off.
4) Quantization impact on perf & quality: used perf deltas from quant-exp/optimize-q8-q4 report. Runtime GPU speedups estimated at 1.3x for q8_0, 1.8x for q4_1 on A10G. We did not include quality regression penalty other than an assumed 0.5% regen rate for q4. Open: product wants to list which customer cohorts are allowed to use aggressive quantization.
5) Cold-start vs warm inference split: warm inference assumed 92% (KV present); cold path includes reruns to populate KV. Data from logs/warm-warm.csv. This assumption has large leverage on per-token cost for short-lived sessions.

Calibration steps executed (short log):
- Pulled Q4-2024 billing + token export and matched per-customer cost to model output for 50 high-volume accounts.
- Tuned batch profile parameters until aggregate cost delta < 8% for hosted API. Dedicated mismatch persisted for 3 accounts due to A100 vs A10G perf differences.
- Ran sensitivity sweeps for KV hit rate (10, 25, 50) and batch-mix (20/80, 40/60, 60/40). Results saved to s3://redwood-optimize/audit/2025-02-08-sensitivity.csv.
- Performed quick quality-check by sampling 200 generated responses under q4 quantization and confirming regression flags in eval-dashboard (manual review by Claire).

Open questions for Finance sign-off (needs a decision before 2025-02-18):
- Ops allocation: is 10% of SRE/Ops justified to allocate to Optimize? Finance suggested 6% historical baseline; product wants 12% because Optimize requires 24/7 coverage for rollouts.
- Discount treatment: should committed Dedicated capacity be amortized over contract length (12 months) or treated as prepaid capex? Affects monthly unit costs.
- Headroom for renewals: do we bake in expected 5% price decrease from GPU supplier renewals in mid-2025? Finance prefers not to assume future price declines unless contracted.
- Contingency for model fallbacks: we assumed 2% fallback to larger model (cost multiplier x1.9) under peak saturation. Should this be included as a recurring multiplier or as a sporadic incident cost bucket?

Mini decision log (who said what):
- 2025-02-05 Miguel: prefer conservative KV hit (25%) until we have broader telemetry.
- 2025-02-07 Elena (Finance): ops allocation should be reconciled with headcount reporting; asked for mapping to payroll buckets.
- 2025-02-09 Claire: flagged quality risk for q4 on generation-heavy LLM tasks; suggested we limit q4 to retrieval-heavy routes.

Sensitivity highlights (numbers are rough, see sweep CSV):
- KV hit from 25% -> 50% reduces per-1M-token cost by ~7–10% depending on model size.
- Batch-mix shift from 80% interactive to 60% interactive increases cost by ~4% (less amortization).
- Switching Dedicated instance types (A10G -> A100) affects throughput per-dollar variance up to 12% for long-context workloads.

Artifact checklist for audit completeness (what to attach to the sign-off packet):
- Billing reconciliation dump for Q4-2024 and Jan-2025 sample (billing-raw.tokens_daily_export and billing/invoices/cust-summaries).
- Perf benchmark suite outputs (perf-runs/2025-01-*/).
- Sensitivity sweep CSV (s3 link above).
- Small-sample quality eval notes (manual-review-q4-sample.md).
- Ops allocation spreadsheet and headcount mapping (finance-infra/ops-attribution-2025.xlsx).

Immediate next steps (owners & ETA):
- [Asha] finalize ops allocation mapping and present to Elena — due 2025-02-11.
- [Miguel] re-run Dedicated perf bench against a representative A100 pool to tighten variance numbers — due 2025-02-12.
- [Claire] expand manual quality sample for q4 to 1k generations and tag fail modes — due 2025-02-14.
- [Elena] provide finance preference on amortization vs prepaid treatment by 2025-02-14.

Notes-to-self and talking points for Finance meeting:
- Emphasize that the primary levers are KV hit rate and batch mixing; small changes cascade into material unit cost differences.
- Be explicit about which assumptions are conservative vs optimistic and why (we should label them in the final memo).
- Ask Finance for policy decisions (ops allocation standard, discount assumptions, and fallback incident accounting) — these are governance items, not modeling minutiae.

Appendix (short gloss on terms used):
- KV cache: per-request key/value cache for attention prefixes that reduces compute by skipping repeated prefixes.
- Batch amortization: token compute cost is amortized across simultaneous requests inside a batch window; higher batch sizes reduce per-token overhead.
- Quantization profiles: runtime encoding that reduces precision to speed up compute; trade-offs with quality vary by model and task.

If you spot any missing artifacts or want a quick slice of the sensitivity sweep to present in the deck, ping me on #product-optimize or drop a quick comment here.

---
Draft ends.
